solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Playgroup?

parts.note: not a nursery for small children but the group of actors who perform in a play

explanation.walkthrough: 'Playgroup' suggests toddlers at a nursery; the question mark invites reading it as the group in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The full company of actors performing in a play is collectively called its cast.

clue.text: Trophy to get on item of furniture

parts.note: a cup is a trophy awarded to winners
to board a bus or ship is to get on it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how to set a prize up on top of a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet with shelves and doors for storage is a standard piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Island finally gets link by bridge

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: An island at last gains a road connection over a new bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the end of each of gets, link, by and bridge. Skye, off Scotland's west coast, really is joined to the mainland by a road bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is one of the largest islands of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Two secretaries do cards initially for old dictator

indicators.note: two signals that the following abbreviation is written twice in succession

parts.note: PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

indicators.note: initially picks out only the opening letter of the word cards

explanation.surface: A pair of office assistants handle the cards for a former tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letter of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa Doc was the nickname of François Duvalier, who ruled Haiti as a brutal dictator from 1957 to 1971.

clue.text: Earth, say, in tree found by tribe's leader

indicators.note: found by places the next piece beside the tree, following it

parts.note: the plane is a broad-leaved tree common in city streets

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of tribe's

explanation.surface: A clue about the earth around a tree, discovered by a tribal chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one example of the worlds that orbit the sun, hence the 'say' marking an example.

clue.text: Open space in taking on poor Fidel

parts.note: to take on an opponent is to play against them

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in bad shape and needs rearranging

explanation.surface: An open space where someone takes on a weakened Fidel Castro.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassed area set aside for sports and games is a large open space.

clue.text: May dread disturbing reverie

indicators.note: disturbing tells us the letters of may dread are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named May finds her pleasant musing troubled by fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a pleasant waking fantasy in which the mind drifts away from reality.

clue.text: Artist denied curate's smart

indicators.note: denied means the artist is refused a place, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the curate, with the 's read as 'is' joining it to the definition
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter is turned away, and the clergyman's assistant looks smart.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing RA from CURATE leaves CUTE; the 's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in American usage means clever or shrewd, a sense shared with sharp-witted.

clue.text: Marksman's new photos held by sharer

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: held by means the rearranged letters sit inside the word sharer
new indicates the letters of photos are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A rifleman's fresh pictures are kept by somebody who shares them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Marksman is read as 'is', a link; 'new' rearranges photos, and 'held by' places that inside sharer.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is a highly skilled shot, exactly what a crack shooter is called.

clue.text: Freud for one confusing calypso with shanty

indicators.note: confusing means the letters of calypso and shanty are mixed up together

explanation.surface: Sigmund Freud is imagined muddling two kinds of song, a Caribbean calypso and a sea shanty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud founded psychoanalysis, so he is the prime example of a practitioner of it.

clue.text: French way to show regret

definitions.meaning: the French word for a street or road
to be sorry for or lament something done

explanation.definitionFit: Rue is the French for street, and in English to rue something is to regret it bitterly.

clue.text: Fabulist initially adopted backward attitude

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of adopted
backward means the word for attitude is written from end to start

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or affected stance

explanation.surface: A storyteller at first took on an old-fashioned outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables, so he is the archetypal writer of such tales.

clue.text: Immigrants from south with letters for translation

indicators.note: for translation suggests the word letters is turned into another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Newcomers from the south bring documents that need translating.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlers are people who move to a new country and make their home there, as immigrants do.

clue.text: Touching line from Brown — polite chap

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
a gent is a gentleman, a courteous man

explanation.surface: A line of conversation from a courteous man called Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it.

clue.text: Deadly place to get off

definitions.meaning: fatal, as of an illness that will end in death
the end station of a bus, rail or air route where passengers alight

explanation.definitionFit: A terminal disease is a fatal one, and a terminal is the final station where travellers disembark.

clue.text: Duke felt strong desire to be thrown out

parts.note: to be itching to do something is to want it badly

explanation.surface: A duke longed to be expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is informally to discard or abandon it.

clue.text: Discover code's cryptic in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone tries to crack a code that is partly obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is an old literary verb meaning to catch sight of or detect something.

clue.text: Father eating bird finds bone

indicators.note: eating means the priest's letters take the bird inside

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A priest dining on poultry comes across a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the longest in the human body.

clue.text: Priest: the Spanish one

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cleric is identified as the Spanish one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who raised the young Samuel, a crossword staple.

clue.text: Try to accommodate new situation that's annoying

indicators.note: to accommodate is to make room for, so the attempt holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: a bid is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to put up with an irritating new state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bind is informal British for a tiresome chore or awkward predicament.

clue.text: Pretentiously sentimental? Time to go!

parts.note: to go, informally, is to urinate, which is also to wee

explanation.surface: Someone sick of mawkish gush announces that it is time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to go!' reads as a call to leave; 'go' is the nursery word for urinating, WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for quaintly cute or affectedly sweet in an irritating way.

clue.text: Double success after Latin edict redrafted

indicators.note: after puts the victory word at the end
redrafted means the words Latin edict are rewritten in another order

parts.note: a win is a success

explanation.surface: A ruling in Latin succeeds after it is rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is someone who looks exactly like another, as a sibling from the same egg does.

clue.text: Ruin of the French city of Paris

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' before a plural noun
Paris was the Trojan prince who carried off Helen, so his city is Troy

explanation.surface: A lament on the ruin of a French city, apparently the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' is not the French capital but the prince of Troy in Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck it completely, which is to demolish or wipe it out.

clue.text: Healthy source of water

definitions.meaning: a shaft sunk into the ground to draw up water

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling fit is being well, and a well is a bored shaft that supplies water.
